overview: A one-page U.S. Department of State list of papers filed under “Coal—Japan,” indexing material from 1940 onward about Japan’s wartime coal supply. The listed records concern domestic coal shortages, coke deliveries from the Netherlands East Indies, coal-conservation measures announced by Deputy Minister Kishi, reports of large reserves in Tungpientao in eastern Manchuria, and an Office of Strategic Services report on the production and transportation of coal to Japan under Japanese administration.

subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Coal—Japan
subfiles.about: An archival index lists reports and correspondence concerning Japan’s coal shortage, imports, conservation measures, reserves, production, and transportation.
subfiles.summary: The sheet indexes a February 15, 1940 report from Joseph C. Grew on Japan’s coal shortage and April 1941 correspondence by Pierrepont W. Parker concerning coke deliveries from the Netherlands East Indies and a related London cable. It also lists two December 23 telegrams from Leland Harrison in Switzerland: one on coal-saving measures announced by Deputy Minister Kishi and another on reported coal reserves of 220 million tons in Tungpientao, eastern Manchuria, as reported by Berlin’s Deutsche Allgemeine. A January 29 Office of Strategic Services item concerns coal production and transportation to Japan under Japanese administration.

interest: The sheet is useful as a compact guide to several related records that connect Japan’s domestic fuel shortage with colonial or overseas supply networks, state conservation policy, and the search for coal reserves in occupied Manchuria. It also shows how information reached the State Department through diplomatic reporting from Tokyo and Switzerland, a London cable, German press reporting, and wartime intelligence. Although the indexed documents themselves are absent, their précis preserve valuable clues for locating related material, including the cross-reference to file 894.50/118.
